prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the pii-chat agent (card support: identity checks, lost and stolen cards, replacements) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: telling the society a policyholder has died. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a caller says a policyholder has died, we should slow the conversation down, acknowledge the bereavement, and keep the wording plain and respectful rather than jumping straight to card closure steps."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a death is reported, I should first confirm the caller’s relationship to the policyholder and only ask for the minimum details needed to log the notification and protect the account."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the caller is upset or unsure who else needs to be informed, I should explain that I can note the death on the record and guide them on the next practical steps without making them repeat the story."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the policyholder has cards in their own name, I should treat any requests for card cancellation or replacement as a separate action from the bereavement note and check authority before proceeding."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there are joint accounts or additional cardholders, I should ask targeted questions about whether the card was solely the deceased person’s or linked to a shared account, so I do not interrupt access unnecessarily."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the caller provides a death certificate or says one will follow, I should record what has been offered and avoid insisting on documents I do not need at that stage."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a death has been reported, I should avoid using phrases that sound like a final decision on the wider estate; my job is to log the notification, protect the account, and pass anything more complex on."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the caller is not the next of kin, I should be careful not to disclose account details and should keep the update limited to confirming that the society can receive the notification and review next steps."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I need to verify identity, I should use the lightest possible check that fits the situation, because bereaved callers may struggle with paperwork or exact dates under stress."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the case may involve linked products, I should remind myself to check whether the death notification needs to be shared across the customer record so other teams can pick it up consistently."}]}
